questions.question: In a CommonJS script, what is the output of `Promise.resolve().then(() => console.log("P")); process.nextTick(() => console.log("N")); console.log("S");`?
questions.explanation: Synchronous code runs first. Then Node drains the process.nextTick queue before the promise microtask queue, so N prints before P.

questions.question: Inside an fs.readFile callback, you schedule both `setTimeout(fn, 0)` and `setImmediate(fn)`. Which runs first?
options: setImmediate, because the check phase follows the poll phase in the same loop turn
setTimeout, because timers always run first
The order is random every time
Neither runs until the file is closed
questions.explanation: I/O callbacks run in the poll phase. The check phase (setImmediate) comes next, while timers are only processed on the next turn of the loop, so the order is deterministic here.

questions.question: Which event loop phase runs setImmediate callbacks?
questions.explanation: The phases are timers, pending callbacks, idle/prepare, poll, check and close callbacks. setImmediate callbacks run in the check phase.

questions.question: A route handler in a Node HTTP server runs a CPU-heavy loop for 3 seconds. What happens to other incoming requests during that time?
options: They are handled in parallel on other JavaScript threads automatically
They wait, because the single main thread cannot run any other callback until the loop finishes
They are rejected with a 503 status by Node
Only requests to the same route wait
questions.explanation: All JavaScript callbacks share one thread, so a blocking operation delays every request. Move CPU work to worker threads or break it into chunks.
